concepts.def: A noble character destroyed by a flaw
Society ruled and dominated by men

walkthroughs.body_html:
Macbeth fits Aristotle's tragic hero mould: noble, with a hamartia (ambition) and hubris (overconfidence after Act 4).

His downfall delivers catharsis — relief mixed with pity.

The Gunpowder Plot (1605) terrified Jacobean audiences.

Macbeth (1606) plays on that fear: regicide brings chaos. Banquo — James's ancestor — represents goodness restored.

Is Lady Macbeth a villain — or a victim of patriarchy?

Her cry "unsex me here" suggests she sees womanhood itself as a cage. Top essays explore this tension.

mcqs.q: A tragic hero's fatal flaw is:
options: hubris
hamartia
catharsis
pathos

mcqs.q: What is the structural framework of The Canterbury Tales?
options: A sonnet must always be exactly ten lines long.
It is a religious text used in Catholic services.
It is one continuous story told by Chaucer from beginning to end.
A frame narrative — pilgrims travelling to Canterbury tell stories along the way, allowing Chaucer to juxtapose different voices, genres and social classes.

mcqs.q: What is the structure of a Shakespearean sonnet?
options: Fourteen lines in iambic pentameter, structured as three quatrains and a final couplet, rhyming ABAB CDCD EFEF GG, often with a volta near the couplet.
A sonnet must always be exactly ten lines long.
A soliloquy is when characters argue with each other.
A sonnet is any short love poem.

mcqs.q: What is the dramatic function of a soliloquy?
options: A soliloquy is any long speech a character gives.
It reveals a character's inner thoughts directly to the audience while the character is alone on stage — a convention granting access to private psychology.
It is a religious text used in Catholic services.
A soliloquy is when characters argue with each other.
